questions.question: A 3-year-old boy is brought to the pediatric emergency department with a 6-day history of high-grade fever unresponsive to antipyretics. On examination, he has non-purulent bilateral conjunctival injection, dry cracked lips with a strawberry tongue, erythema and desquamation of the periungual regions of his hands, and tender right anterior cervical lymphadenopathy. Laboratory studies show leukocytosis and an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate. Which of the following is the most appropriate initial medical therapy to prevent long-term cardiac complications in this patient?
options: Intravenous pulse methylprednisolone with high-dose ibuprofen

questions.question: A 34-year-old forestry worker presents with a 4-day history of headache, neck stiffness, low-grade fever, and acute bilateral facial nerve weakness. History reveals he noticed an expanding, target-like rash on his thigh three weeks after a tick bite while working in Connecticut two months ago. Lumbar puncture demonstrates a lymphocytic pleocytosis, elevated protein, and normal glucose. CSF Lyme antibodies are positive. Which of the following is the first-line intravenous therapy for central nervous system involvement in this patient?

A 28-year-old woman with a history of relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis is being evaluated for initiation of disease-modifying therapy. Her neurologist considers prescribing natalizumab. Which of the following best describes the molecular mechanism of action of this medication?
options: Inhibition of dihydroorotate dehydrogenase, blocking pyrimidine synthesis in activated T cells
Monoclonal antibody blockade of the alpha-4 integrin subunit, preventing leukocyte extravasation across the blood-brain barrier
Sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) receptor modulation, causing internalisation of receptors and lymph node sequestration
Selective depletion of CD20-positive B lymphocytes via complement-dependent cytotoxicity

questions.question: A 55-year-old man presents with progressive generalized swelling and heavy foamy urine over the past 3 weeks. Physical examination shows bilateral 3+ pitting lower extremity edema. Laboratory testing reveals 24-hour urinary protein excretion of 5.2 g/day, serum albumin of 2.1 g/dL, and total cholesterol of 380 mg/dL. Renal biopsy exhibits subepithelial immune complex deposition with a 'spike and dome' appearance on silver stain. Which of the following autoantibodies is most specific for the primary form of this patient's condition?

A 68-year-old man presents for a routine eye exam. Tonometry reveals an intraocular pressure (IOP) of 27 mmHg in the right eye and 26 mmHg in the left eye (normal: 10–21 mmHg). Fundoscopic examination reveals asymmetric optic disc cupping with a cup-to-disc ratio of 0.7 on the right. Gonioscopy confirms open, unobstructed anterior chamber angles in both eyes. The patient is prescribed latanoprost ophthalmic drops. What is the primary mechanism of action by which this medication lowers intraocular pressure?
options: Decreasing aqueous humor production via selective alpha-2 adrenergic receptor stimulation
Increasing uveoscleral outflow of aqueous humor
Decreasing aqueous humor production via inhibition of carbonic anhydrase in the ciliary body
Direct contraction of the ciliary muscle to mechanically open the trabecular meshwork
